claims.statement: A plan proposal escalates straight into the plan gate on submission (delivery is the gate), while `proposal.accept` only handles development proposals — so accepting a plan proposal is refused with a hint to use `gate.approve`.
`gate.approve` requires the gate revision to equal the requirement revision (`gate_rev == req.rev`); a mismatch is reported as stale and blocks approval, so an amend always forces re-verification.

All three rejections — proposal, gate and integration — land the requirement back in `ready` with `plan_ok` preserved and the lane released; only an amend that invalidates `plan_ok` forces the plan gate to be re-run.

Green means literal evidence: the workspace tests, the `egg` example tests and the `selftest` run must each be run verbatim with their exit codes recorded; a member-equivalent run such as `cargo check` or an `--filter` selection proves only that substitute, never the suite.
A gate is not trusted until a mutation probe shows it can go red: putting the old semantics back must fail the assertion, otherwise the assertion is vacuous.
The wasm build deliberately avoids wasm-pack because it cannot pass `wasm-bindgen --reference-types`; the chain is fixed as cargo plus the wasm-bindgen CLI in two steps.
